deep_subsidy_income_limits_cad.effective: 2026 (1 Aug to 31 Jul for Community Housing Fund projects)

tiers.market: 30% of homes: an initial market rent approved by BC Housing, kept at or above CMHC's average market rent; tenants under the low- and moderate-income limits, chosen by the operator; proof of income at move-in only
tiers.rgi: 50% of homes: rent by BC Housing's Rent Scale (the Rent Calculation Guide); tenants with an income below the Housing Income Limits, chosen from The Housing Registry; proof of income and assets every year
tiers.deep_subsidy: 20% of homes: rent by the Rent Scale; residents with an income below the Deep Subsidy Income Limits, chosen from The Housing Registry; proof of income and assets every year

params.not_read_from_bc_housing: the mix tolerance of 2 points is this tool's own rounding rule: no call document read gives one
params.financing: interim construction and take-out financing up to 100% of the construction cost of the housing, by BC Housing's lending criteria; the take-out loan is CMHC-insured and amortized over 35 years
params.operating_subsidy: limited, where required: the shortfall between the approved rental revenue and the approved operating costs, mortgage payments included
params.tenure_not_accepted: a premises lease or a sublease (CMHC does not accept either for financing)
params.rgi_rent_estimate: the 2023 call's Appendix 12 estimates rent-geared-to-income revenue on tenants averaging 70% of the Housing Income Limit, and deep-subsidy revenue on the income assistance shelter allowance (rule f.rgi_rents)

takeout_financing.for: non-profits, co-ops and public housing corporations

params.who_may_apply: co-op or non-profit developers, public housing corporations, First Nations developers and private developers; a non-profit that wants to own and operate teams with a developer or builder, for-profit or non-profit (operators alone are not sought)
params.grants: for buildings owned and operated by co-op or non-profit developers and First Nations controlled development corporations, to reach at least 20% of the homes at 20% below market rents
params.capital_grant_terms: for a limited number of homes in select non-profit projects; at least 20% of the homes at 20% below market for 35 years; the homes owned and run by a non-profit provider, a public housing corporation or a First Nations-controlled development corporation; secured by a 35-year forgivable mortgage and a Section 219 covenant
params.operating_subsidy: none: the project must run without any operating subsidy from BC Housing
params.interim_financing: up to 100% of the cost to complete the project, by BC Housing's lending criteria

rules.title: BC Housing Indigenous Housing Fund: who it is for

params.what: affordable rental homes for Indigenous families, Elders, individuals and people with disabilities, on and off reserve; every home rent geared to income (fixed rents may be considered on reserve)

params.how_a_project_enters: by BC Housing's request for proposals

rules.title: BC Housing Supportive Housing Fund: who it is for

params.what: subsidized housing with 24/7 on-site support services for people experiencing or at risk of homelessness, with a household income at or below the Housing Income Limits; adults first, families and youth where approved
params.funds: the whole capital cost, and afterwards an operating subsidy (approved expenses less revenue) and a support-services subsidy set by the approved staff schedule
params.how_a_project_enters: through BC Housing rather than by a society's grant application: BC Housing works with municipalities and other landowners to secure a site, procures and builds the housing, and signs an operator agreement with a non-profit (three to five years, with an option for five more)
params.intake: not stated on the program page (read 23 Nov 2026)
params.owner: the Provincial Rental Housing Corporation, the Province's land-holding company, in full; a non-profit operates the building
params.rents: rent geared to income for every home; a resident on income assistance pays the maximum shelter component, and some projects set a flat rent
params.cross_subsidy: none: the project must be financially viable by itself

rules.title: BC Housing Women's Transition Housing Fund: who it is for

params.what: housing with supports for women and their children who are at risk of, or have experienced, violence, in four streams: safe homes (stays of about 10 days), transition houses (about 30 days), second-stage housing (up to about 18 months) and long-term rental housing
params.funds: 1,500 new homes from 2018, and the service agreement each provider runs them under
params.how_a_project_enters: by agreement with BC Housing: the framework names no application route, so ask BC Housing
params.intake: not stated on the program page (read 23 Nov 2026)
params.owner: the Provincial Rental Housing Corporation for the buildings and land created under the fund, leased to non-profit societies and co-operatives
params.rents: 30% of income in second-stage and long-term rental housing, by BC Housing's rent scale; a resident on income assistance pays the maximum shelter component
params.incomes: low and moderate incomes for second-stage housing; at or below the Housing Income Limits for long-term rental housing

rules.title: BC Housing HEARTH (Homeless Encampment Action Response Temporary Housing): how it works

params.what: new shelter and temporary housing spaces for people who are unsheltered or living in encampments
params.funds: the operating cost of shelter and temporary housing sites in the communities the Province picks: program staff, direct program and support services, property management and administration, on a budget negotiated each year under agreements of up to three years
params.how_a_project_enters: not by application: the Ministry of Housing, with BC Housing, picks priority communities and may sign a memorandum of understanding with the municipality; BC Housing then manages the procurement and chooses the non-profit operator. Ask the City whether it has one
params.intake: not an application program: communities are selected by the Province
params.rents: at a temporary housing site a fixed rent at the maximum shelter component of income assistance, or a rent geared to income under the operator agreement; at a shelter site none
params.incomes: at or below the Housing Income Limits

rules.title: BC Housing Emergency Shelter Program: what a shelter is under it

params.what: year-round, temporary (winter included) and extreme-weather shelters for anyone homeless or at risk of homelessness; a bed, meals, showers, laundry and support staff, free of charge; year-round shelters staffed 24 hours a day
params.funds: running a shelter, not building one: BC Housing pays the provider's eligible program costs (program staff, direct program expenses, property management and administration) on an operating budget negotiated with each provider
params.how_a_project_enters: by a support services agreement with BC Housing; the framework names no open application, and extreme-weather shelters sit under a separate framework
params.intake: not stated on the page read (23 Nov 2026)
params.rents: none: funded services are free to the people who use them
params.access: 24 hours a day, seven days a week unless BC Housing approves otherwise; a bed for each client; separate, secure sleeping spaces where a shelter serves more than one group

rules.title: City of Vancouver Community Housing Incentive Program (CHIP): who it is for

params.what: a City grant toward building non-market housing, for non-profit and co-op organizations building on their own land in Vancouver; stream 1 for self-sustaining projects that leverage senior-government funding, stream 2 for deeply affordable projects that rely on senior-government operating subsidies
params.funds: a capital grant, funded by the Empty Homes Tax
params.how_a_project_enters: by the City's funding call, then Council approves each grant
params.intake: closed: no funding call is open at this time (program page, read 23 Nov 2026)
params.amounts_unverified: the 2025 call's maximums were reported as $10,000 a home at the Housing Income Limits and $25,000 a home at the shelter rate in stream 2, and up to $65,000 a home in stream 1's 2024 call (from the City's guidelines as a search summarised them; not read here and not counted in the money)

rules.title: Reaching Home (Canada's Homelessness Strategy): capital investments

params.what: capital for emergency shelters, transitional housing and supportive housing that serve only people experiencing or at imminent risk of homelessness, paired with wrap-around services; planning must show financial sustainability and services for at least five years after completion
params.funds: capital, alongside other funders: it cannot duplicate or displace other funding or exceed 100% of eligible costs
params.how_a_project_enters: through the region's Community Entity, by its calls for proposals
params.intake: by call for proposals from the Community Entity; none was read here
params.community_entity_unverified: for Greater Vancouver the Community Entity was reported as Lu'ma Native Housing Society with Vancity Community Foundation (a search summary of their pages; confirm with them)
